variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: LLM inference optimization is the engineering work that makes an already-trained language model respond within a product's latency, capacity, cost, and quality limits. It changes how requests are admitted, batched, cached, scheduled, represented in memory, and decoded; it does not retrain the model's core knowledge.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Prefill
pairs.detail: The model processes many input tokens in parallel.
pairs.explanation: The model processes many input tokens in parallel. Long prompts create substantial arithmetic work, while exact prefix reuse can skip already-computed blocks.

pairs.label: Decode
pairs.detail: Autoregressive generation produces one next-token step at a time.
pairs.explanation: Autoregressive generation produces one next-token step at a time. The scheduler repeatedly reads model weights and each sequence's growing KV state.

pairs.label: Shared serving pool
pairs.detail: Prefill bursts can delay interactive decode, while too many active sequences can exhaust KV memory.
pairs.explanation: Prefill bursts can delay interactive decode, while too many active sequences can exhaust KV memory. Scheduling policy decides who waits.

variants.hint:
Prefill: The model processes many input tokens in parallel.

Decode: Autoregressive generation produces one next-token step at a time.

Shared serving pool: Prefill bursts can delay interactive decode, while too many active sequences can exhaust KV memory.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: BF16 or FP16 baseline
pairs.detail: Keep a measured reference checkpoint and engine path.
pairs.explanation: Keep a measured reference checkpoint and engine path. It anchors task quality, numerical behavior, memory, latency, and rollback comparisons.

pairs.label: INT8 or FP8
pairs.detail: Weights and possibly activations use fewer bits.
pairs.explanation: Weights and possibly activations use fewer bits. Kernel and hardware support determine whether fewer bytes become lower latency or higher throughput.

pairs.label: INT4 weight-only
pairs.detail: Methods such as AWQ or GPTQ can reduce weight storage substantially, but calibration, task quality, kernel support, and dequantization overhead remain workload-specific.
pairs.explanation: Methods such as AWQ or GPTQ can reduce weight storage substantially, but calibration, task quality, kernel support, and dequantization overhead remain workload-specific.

pairs.label: Speculative decoding
pairs.detail: A cheaper drafter proposes several tokens and the target verifies them in parallel.
pairs.explanation: A cheaper drafter proposes several tokens and the target verifies them in parallel. Speed depends on acceptance, draft cost, target batch size, and implementation.
